  \caption{Native end-to-end proofs of $N$ multiplications $x \cdot y = z$ of random $64$-bit integers ($z$ a $128$-bit integer; from $2^{21}$ the \ftwoz\ layout caps its row side at $t = 18$, which trades read-off bytes for prover time): \ftwoz\ (integer R1CS, Lambda100; Ligerito rate $1/2$ is Johnson, custom:1:4, early Round-0 OOD; rate $1/8$ is Johnson, custom:3:4, early Round-0 OOD), Binius64 (native multiplication, ring switching and BaseFold at rate $1/2$ with $241$ queries and rate $1/8$ with $121$ queries for $100$ bits), Binius64 with the \ftwoz\ opener (the same circuit and PIOP; every oracle committed and opened by ring switching and Johnson-regime Ligerito with Round~0 at rate $1/2$ with $194$ level-0 queries, $16--21$ bits of fold grinding and a $105$-bit per-round target ($100.2--100.4$ bits achieved; the round-by-round minimum is $105.0$ bits) and at rate $1/8$ with $63$ level-0 queries, $17--22$ bits of fold grinding and a $105$-bit per-round target ($100.3--100.6$ bits achieved; the round-by-round minimum is $105.0--105.1$ bits); the whole-protocol figure is a union bound over every error term, gated at $100$ bits), and Binius64 with the \ftwoz\ opener (the same circuit and PIOP; every oracle committed and opened by ring switching and Johnson-regime Ligerito with Round~0 at rate $1/2$ with $183$ level-0 queries, $11--16$ bits of fold grinding and a $100$-bit per-round target ($100.0$ bits achieved; the union bound over the same terms is $95.3--95.4$ bits) and at rate $1/8$ with $60$ level-0 queries, $12--17$ bits of fold grinding and a $100$-bit per-round target ($100.0--100.1$ bits achieved; the union bound over the same terms is $95.5--95.7$ bits); every error term is gated at $100$ bits on its own, the round-by-round minimum the \ftwoz\ rows report). Native security targets are reported separately; these are not a uniform complete-protocol bound. \emph{Witgen} is the native witness generation; \emph{prover} is the complete prover call after witness generation, commitment included; \emph{verifier} is the complete verification; \emph{peak mem.} is the high-water resident set of a separate child process proving and verifying once ($1$\,GB $= 2^{30}$ bytes). Binius64 at rate $1/2$ was not run at $2^{23}$. Binius64 at rate $1/8$ was not run at $2^{23}$. Binius64 with the \ftwoz\ opener (union bound) at rate $1/2$ was not run at $2^{21}$, $2^{22}$, $2^{23}$. Binius64 with the \ftwoz\ opener (union bound) at rate $1/8$ was not run at $2^{21}$, $2^{22}$, $2^{23}$. Binius64 with the \ftwoz\ opener (round-by-round) at rate $1/2$ was not run at $2^{21}$, $2^{22}$, $2^{23}$. Binius64 with the \ftwoz\ opener (round-by-round) at rate $1/8$ was not run at $2^{21}$, $2^{22}$, $2^{23}$. The prover's working set exceeds the machine's memory for \ftwoz\ at rate $1/2$ at $2^{23}$, \ftwoz\ at rate $1/8$ at $2^{23}$, Binius64 at rate $1/2$ at $2^{22}$, and Binius64 at rate $1/8$ at $2^{22}$, so those rows are reported but paging-dominated and are not comparable with the rest. Apple M5; threads per run: 8; medians of 5 runs after one warm-up.}
